stances.claim: After three consecutive non-career SC appointments (Leonen, Jardeleza, Caguioa) -- all eminently deserving -- institutional balance now requires giving career jurists their chance to rise, and the JBC wisely nominated career jurists only for the first slot to enable this rebalancing.
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-balance argument with disclosure of CJ's own JBC consultant recommendation

stances.claim: Independence and integrity are the most critical of the four constitutional traits (competence, integrity, probity, independence) because the high court is the last bastion of democracy -- expected to protect constitutional rights against executive and legislative abuse of authority -- and all presidents naturally appoint justices they believe will uphold their program.

Industry should be added as a desired trait given the SC's 8,000-case backlog producing an average 533 cases per justice plus 40 new cases per month -- to keep up with incoming load each justice must decide 40 per month plus many more to reduce backlog, making industriousness a structural requirement, not optional.
stances.rhetorical_move: additional-trait argument with quantified workload justification

notable_anecdotes: CJ's disclosure that he is a JBC consultant who specifically recommended career-jurist nominations for the first slot -- making his analysis institutionally grounded rather than external commentary.
The arithmetic of SC workload: '8,000 divided by 15 equals 533' -- using simple division to physicalize the backlog crisis per justice.

Tessie Sy Coson -- chair of BDO and SM Group top leader, just named MAP Management Man of the Year -- preferring to call her former commercial law professor 'professor' rather than 'chief justice,' the column's most personally affectionate vignette.

Henry Sy Sr.'s late-1960s veto of Tessie's law-school dream -- asking her instead to help run the 'then modest ShoeMart store in downtown Manila' -- which 50 years later became 'the largest business conglomerate in our country' and made him a $16B+ wealthiest Filipino.

CJ's gentle deflection of Tessie's lawyer-envy: 'as the head of the biggest bank and as a top boss of the largest conglomerate here, she can retain and direct the best and brightest practicing lawyers in the country and in the world without having to be one' -- the most economical statement of corporate-vs-legal-career tradeoff in the column.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Judicial and Bar Council's nominees for the first two of twelve Supreme Court vacancies during President Duterte's six-year term, opening December 16 and 29, 2016. He discloses that as a JBC consultant he recommended career-jurist nominations only for the first slot -- to balance the Court's composition after three consecutive non-career appointments (Marvic Leonen, Francis Jardeleza, Alfredo Caguioa) -- and the JBC wisely complied: the first-slot nominees are CA Justices Apolinario Bruselas Jr., Japar Dimaampao, PJ Andres Reyes Jr., Jose Reyes Jr., and Sandiganbayan Justice Samuel Martires. The second slot opens to a wider field including CA Justices Rosmari Carandang, Amy Lazaro-Javier, Noel Tijam, and lawyer Rita Linda Jimeno. He reviews the constitutional qualifications (natural-born, 40+, 15+ years' service or practice) and the four 'proven competence, integrity, probity and independence' traits -- arguing that independence and integrity are most critical because the SC is 'the last bastion of democracy,' and that industry should be added as a desired trait given the 8,000-case backlog (533 per justice on average, plus 40 new cases raffled per justice per month). He closes with a personal tribute to Tessie Sy Coson -- BDO chair, SM Group top leader, newly named MAP Management Man of the Year -- recalling her as his late-1960s commercial law student at Assumption Convent whose lawyer-dream her father Henry Sy Sr. vetoed in favor of running 'their then modest ShoeMart store,' which 50 years later became the country's largest business conglomerate and made Henry the wealthiest Filipino at $16B+ net worth. Tessie still calls CJ 'professor' rather than 'chief justice,' to which he replies that as BDO chair and SM Group leader 'she can retain and direct the best and brightest practicing lawyers in the country and in the world without having to be one.'
